input.prompt:
One continuous ten-second locked-off tripod shot at the existing workshop table. The camera does not move: no pan, tilt, zoom, drift, follow or reframing, and no cuts. The background stays exactly as in the frame. Preserve the supplied starting frame's exact owner and buyer, faces, hair, glasses, tan work shirt, steel-blue overshirt, daylight, room, table, green binder, sheet, pencil and keys. Owner seated screen left, buyer seated screen right.

For the first three seconds both stay seated as in the frame, looking at the sheet, with only breathing and a blink. At about three seconds the buyer looks up at the owner, gives a small polite nod and reaches his right hand across the table. She looks up and takes it. They shake hands once, briefly and courteously, over the table for about a second and a half, then let go. His expression is polite and regretful, not pleased. After releasing her hand he places both hands on the table edge, pushes his chair back and slowly begins to stand, still facing the table. By the end he is rising or just upright beside his chair, about to turn away. The owner stays seated, hands returning near the sheet, eyes following him up.

No smiling celebration, no second handshake, no hug, no speaking, no lip movement, no head shake, no pointing, no papers exchanged, nothing taken from the table. The sheet stays unreadable. No new person, prop, text or sound. Real-time motion.
